research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic official-source research confidence only. Current Planning Data, GOV.UK/MHCLG and Forestry Commission sources checked on 25 July 2026. TPO service records, conservation-area tree controls, felling licences, forestry public registers, UKFS, forestry EIA and hedgerow notices remain at their published legal, policy or dataset scope. They are not parcel-title boundaries, arboricultural surveys, tree-work consent, felling permission for a specific tree, planning permission or Future Growth score accuracy.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification across Planning Data, GOV.UK and Forestry Commission; TPO/felling/hedgerow/forestry-EIA regimes kept distinct; repository collision check before publication.

source_facts.fact: Planning Data reports 107,674 Tree Preservation Orders from 74 providers; collector last ran and new data was found on 24 July 2026; origin warning says some MHCLG-created data remains pending authoritative replacement.
source_facts.gate: Service records are planning-screening evidence and not a tree survey, consent decision or complete national legal register.

source_facts.fact: New Forestry Commission guidance published 8 July 2026 says a felling licence is generally needed to fell growing trees in England unless an exemption applies.
source_facts.gate: Licence requirement and exemptions must be checked for the actual work; they are not inferred from parcel land use.

source_facts.fact: The Forestry Commission consultation register normally provides a 21-day comment period for relevant forestry proposals, subject to stated exemptions.
source_facts.gate: Presence or absence on the public register is not itself a permission or prohibition for a specific tree.

source_facts.fact: TPO guidance recognises an exception where tree work is carried out in compliance with a Forestry Act 1967 felling licence.
source_facts.gate: A generic TPO record does not override or prove the existence of a valid felling licence; the actual permission must be checked.

source_facts.fact: GOV.UK countryside hedgerow guidance gives the local planning authority 42 days to respond to a written removal notice.
source_facts.gate: The 42-day process is not automatic consent on submission and must not be converted into a planning permission outcome.

source_facts.fact: Forestry Commission constraints guidance updated 15 June 2026 says national mapping tools do not show every constraint, specifically noting TPOs and conservation areas as examples not fully nationally mapped.
source_facts.gate: No national-map non-match may be promoted as proof that a parcel has no tree constraint.

core_rules: TPO service record is not an arboricultural survey
TPO point or polygon data must not be treated as title boundary
absence from Planning Data TPO service does not prove no TPO exists
Planning Data TPO origin warning must be preserved
TPO designation is not automatic refusal of development
TPO status does not itself determine whether specific tree work is acceptable
conservation-area tree controls are distinct from TPO controls
section 211 notice requirements must not be inferred without checking applicable exemptions
a felling licence is distinct from planning permission
a felling licence is distinct from TPO consent unless a specific legal exception applies
felling-licence exemption must be evidenced for the actual work
dangerous-tree exception must not be assumed without evidence of immediate risk
dead-tree exception must not be inferred from aerial imagery alone
felling licence does not establish ownership or title rights
approved felling does not prove restocking conditions have been discharged
restocking conditions can bind later owners and must not be ignored
Forestry Commission public-register listing is not approval
absence from the consultation register can reflect an exemption and is not proof no licence exists
21-day forestry consultation period is not a planning consultation period
UK Forestry Standard compliance is not planning permission
UKFS is a management standard and not a parcel development score
woodland management plan approval is not a development-plan allocation
forestry EIA stage 1 is not stage 2 consent
forestry EIA afforestation and deforestation regimes must remain distinct
forestry EIA road and quarry projects require their own scope checks
low-risk forestry land is not no-risk development land
Forestry Commission map tools do not show every constraint
TPO and conservation-area absence from national forestry maps must not be inferred
local records checks remain necessary where nationally unmapped constraints may exist
hedgerow protection is distinct from TPO protection
hedgerow removal notice is not planning permission
42-day hedgerow response period is not automatic approval on submission
important hedgerow status must not be guessed from age or appearance alone
private garden hedges and countryside hedgerows must not be conflated
hedgerow tree controls can require separate TPO conservation-area or felling checks
hedgerow permission does not remove wildlife-law obligations
tree-felling permission does not remove SSSI or protected-species obligations
forestry consultation comments do not themselves decide an application
decision-register publication is evidence of a decision only for the recorded forestry case
historic forestry decision must not be shown as current permission after expiry
woodland presence does not prove development prohibition
tree canopy imagery does not prove legal protection
tree-loss estimate must not be fabricated without survey or authoritative geometry
planning condition requiring tree retention is distinct from a TPO
NO_DATA must not be converted into no tree or hedgerow constraint
screening evidence must remain separate from candidate promotion
no parcel tree-work consent planning outcome or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research-source confidence must not be reported as parcel accuracy
